title: every-boundary-crossing-lands-in-the-logs-tree
intention: When something goes wrong, the picture of what just happened is already on disk. Every component logs its major boundary crossings and state changes - an inference call starting, a probe firing at a gate crossing, never every function call or every heartbeat - to one durable logs tree at ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/, whose interior mirrors the code tree. The diagnostic_inspector reads that tree as its prebuild-for-debugging surface, and one deletion against one root forgets everything older than 30 days.
why: AKIEN, 2026-08-18, verbatim: 'logs are indeed the very next thing we have to look at. because we don't have any. and we should have lots... every single everyting is supposed to log major boundry crossings and state changes... the logs are the picture of what just happened when we have a problem... i went straight from ground loop to things much higher up because i was an idiot and just assumed this part was working.' MEASURED THE SAME DAY, and it refines his claim rather than merely confirming it: the corpus already TRIES to log lots. 14 devices stand in class-space; 15 components already call emit() at boundary crossings (bus, trouble, tester, librarian, web_server, sudo_relay, system_rackmount, intention_extractor, ground_loop, charter/projector, build_inspector...); and there are exactly 3 production set_diagnostic_receiver sites, only 2 of them a disk sink, BOTH inside cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/__main__.py. So exactly TWO trails exist on disk - ~/.cairn/devices/bus/0/diagnostics.jsonl (311 lines) and ~/.cairn/devices/cairn/machines/ground_loop/0/diagnostics.jsonl (168 lines). Every other component's emissions are HELD IN MEMORY by DiagnosticBase (the receiver defaults to None) and die with the process, and nothing anywhere is loud about that. THE LIVED SYMPTOM is the one Akien names: a mind arriving at a red has no picture of what just happened, so it re-explores - which is the exact cost diagnostic_inspector's charter exists to remove ('save you tokens in exploring the issue in the same way the prebuild step does for coding'). THE DEFECT IN ONE SENTENCE: wiring the sink is a per-__main__ courtesy instead of physics, so logging is opt-in per assembly point and almost nothing opted in.
traces_to: Law 7 (errors are loud at diagnostic surfaces - DiagnosticBase was born from system_rackmount going red 2/5 SILENTLY, with no assertion and no trace, and a surface that holds its records in memory until the process dies is that same silence one layer along). Law 3 (nothing is known until measured - the emission IS the measurement, and an emission that never reaches disk is a measurement taken and discarded). Law 1 via diagnostic_inspector's charter (the prebuild analog for debugging: the resolver spent only on the novel diagnosis, never on a second exploration to gather what the first pass should have carried). Law 4 (a rule that matters is enforced by physics - 'everything logs its boundary crossings' is prose today and opt-in per assembly point, which is exactly the IOU shape). And the standing intention I-complete-diagnostic-on-first-pass.

falsifier.proves_green: code-seam invariant, transcribed: PROVED, and feeds-back-to-origin-on-failure (Laws 3 + 8). PROVE GATE: the tester runs the proofs beside each touched component - cairn/tools/base/ for the address and the floor receiver, cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/ for the reader half - with at least one tooth a hollow build could not pass: a device instantiated with NO wiring act whose emission is then found ON DISK by reading the file, never by asking the object whether it logged. WATCH GATE: WATCHME(every_boundary_crossing_lands_in_the_logs_tree), spec in `watchme`, probe armed at the berth it names. PARENT GATE: the FIVE children prove before this parent crosses PROVED. THE COUNT HAS NOW DRIFTED TWICE AT THIS SEAM (THREE-to-FOUR on 2026-08-18, FOUR-to-FIVE on 2026-08-19) because it is spelled as a word in two fields and derived from nothing - a hand-maintained count beside the list it counts. Both spellings were corrected by the cast that changed them rather than at a crossing, which is luck and not a mechanism.
falsifier.proves_red: DONE when (1) a device instance that nobody wired writes its boundary crossings to disk on its first run - the coverage measure being trails-on-disk against components-that-emit, standing at 2 against 15 the day this was cast; (2) starting an inference call leaves a log entry, Akien's own named example, which cannot happen today at all; (3) a probe firing at a gate crossing leaves one; (4) the trails resolve under one root, ~/.cairn/logs/<device>/<instance>/, addressed through the one owner and never hand-spelled; (5) deleting everything over 30 days old is ONE deletion against ONE root, crossing no device's gate. WRONG INTENT if: the trails exist and diagnostic_inspector still needs a second exploration to diagnose a red (logging happened, the picture did not - the grain was wrong); or the tree grows write-only with no reader ever firing, which is the slates' measured 96-stored-against-1-read shape re-happening on disk and would mean the inspector's remit went unbought.
falsifier.horizon: the next red that sends a mind looking for what just happened - the event that reliably tests whether the picture is there - and no later than the inference-ticket reshape, which berths its task ticket in this tree and therefore cannot land honestly before it.

how: WIRE, DO NOT BUILD - the parts exist and are proven, and the frame 'build logging' was wrong. The emit surface is cairn/tools/base/diagnostic.py (DiagnosticBase, composed into BaseDevice so emit() is structural for every device). The durable sink is BreadcrumbLog (cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector/log.py, ticket a-record-reaches-disk, 2026-08-12). The reader is cairn/machines/diagnostic_inspector, whose charter already carries Akien's prebuild-for-debugging remit verbatim. Four seams, in dependency order, one per child: (1) the logs tree gains an address at the one owner; (2) a device's emissions reach disk by construction rather than by a wiring call - the physics, Law 4; (3) inference_domain gains an emitter so an inference call starting can log at all (today: zero emit sites); (4) the tree forgets after 30 days by one deletion against one root. MEASURED AND LOAD-BEARING for (2): lowering the writer to the floor is import-legal - log.py imports exactly json, pathlib and cairn.tools.base.address, so its only non-stdlib dependency IS the floor, and diagnostic.py's boot-order law ('stdlib only, no DB, no loguru, no sink backend') forbids a backend, not a json-lines append.
